stem:
Firoz's scores are $12$, $15$, and $18$, so the mean is $15$. He subtracts $4$ from every score.

Which claim correctly states what happens to the mean?

options.text: The new mean is $11$, because every value falls by $4$ so the mean falls by $4$.
The new mean stays $15$, because the gaps between the scores are unchanged.
The new mean is $11$ only when exactly one of the three scores is reduced by $4$.
The answer is the phrase fixed subtraction, with no new mean computed.

teacher.key_rationale: Subtracting 4 from every value subtracts 4 from the mean: 15−4=11. Unchanged gaps omit the shared shift; requiring only one score to move is the wrong scope; naming the phrase alone is not the mean.
